body:
WHAT
Promote turns a local override into the shipped default. POST /api/promote/<id> finds the prompt's default text as a string literal in the engine's TypeScript sources (searching backtick, single and double quote forms and both LF and CRLF line endings), replaces it with the new text in the file's own line-ending style, runs the TypeScript build, and if the build fails writes the original file back. On success it updates the in-memory default and deletes the now-redundant override file.

WHY
A tuned prompt on one machine does not reach anyone else until it is in source; and a prompt edit must never leave the repository uncompilable or silently mangle a literal that could not be found exactly.

WHERE
tools/prompt-lab/server.mjs — promote(id,text), locateLiteral(defaultText), toSourceLiteral(text,quote), withEol(text,eol), QUOTES, sourceFiles() (mtime-signature cache), promotable()/promotableCache, tscBuild(), setPromptDefault and clearPromptOverride from engine/protocol/src/prompts.ts, and the POST '/api/promote/' route returning 200 or 409.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Given a temp copy of a .ts file containing a single-quoted default with an apostrophe (e.g. 'don\'t') and a registry whose defaultText is "don't", locateLiteral finds it (quote "'") and does not report 'no verbatim match'.
2. Given a CRLF file holding a multi-line template literal, locateLiteral reports eol '\r\n', and after promote the file still has CRLF everywhere and the only byte difference from the original is inside the literal.
3. When the needle is a prefix of a longer literal (source drifted ahead), locateLiteral skips that position (the char after the needle is not the closing quote) and returns ok:false rather than replacing a prefix.
4. With tscBuild stubbed to reject, promote writes the new literal, then restores the file so its bytes equal the original, and returns {ok:false, reverted:true, reason starting 'typecheck failed'}; with tscBuild resolving, promote returns {ok:true, file:<relative path>}, the override .txt is deleted and promptCatalog() shows the new defaultText.
5. promote(id,' ') returns 'refusing to promote empty text', an unknown id returns 'unknown prompt id', and two identical literals in source return the 'too ambiguous' reason, none of them touching any file; a replacement containing '$&' is inserted literally (function replacer), not expanded.
